name: Liver care day
remarks: Generated by scripts/build_liver_modules.py; edit synthea/liver_model.json or the compiler.
All numeric laboratory endpoints, time constants, complication probabilities, and outcome probabilities are illustrative synthetic parameters, not fitted clinical estimates.
Outcome probabilities apply once per completed 24-hour model step, conditional on etiology and current severity; they are not annual risks or transplant eligibility criteria.
Severity is a synthetic acute functional impairment index from 0 to 1, separate from hepatocyte injury activity and chronic baseline abnormalities.

Candidacy, graft availability, rejection, timing, laboratory, and outcome parameters remain synthetic assumptions. Only the aggregate ICU-to-transplant target is fitted to the user-defined scenario, not observed MedStar outcomes.
Candidacy is drawn once per evaluation; graft availability is drawn once per completed waiting day after competing clinical outcomes. Alcohol-use status alone never determines candidacy.

There is no forced recovery/death horizon or automatic waitlist expiry. Daily competing outcomes continue; an observation cutoff must be reported as censoring, never converted into a clinical outcome. This is an inpatient waiting model, not a longitudinal outpatient waitlist.

Continuous organ support is represented by device and medication intervals, with care plans and instantaneous procedure markers; surgery is a timed procedure. Devices retain timestamp precision where Synthea care-plan CSVs retain only dates. No ICU-specific encounter class or hospital transfers are introduced.

One optional mild rejection episode at the first outpatient visit resolves under a simplified treatment/monitoring course. Drug product strengths and levels are synthetic record content, not a prescribing protocol.
